title: CTS Unit 9 — Healing, Miracles, and Spiritual Warfare / La sanidad, los milagros y la guerra espiritual

blocks.en: Pentecostalism & the Charismatic Movement · Unit 9
blocks.es_reference: El pentecostalismo y el movimiento carismático · Unidad 9

blocks.en: Healing, Miracles, and Spiritual Warfare
blocks.es_reference: La sanidad, los milagros y la guerra espiritual

blocks.en: A Biblical Study · New King James Version
blocks.es_reference: Un estudio bíblico · Reina-Valera Gómez

blocks.en: "For I am the LORD who heals you."Exodus 15:26 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Porque yo soy Jehová tu Sanador."Éxodo 15:26 (RVG)

blocks.en: Learning Objectives
blocks.es_reference: Objetivos de aprendizaje

blocks.en: Affirm from Scripture that God heals and that the gift of healing is real, and that the church is to pray for the sick.
blocks.es_reference: Afirmar desde la Escritura que Dios sana y que el don de sanidad es real, y que la iglesia ha de orar por los enfermos.

blocks.en: Reject the distortion that healing is guaranteed to every believer whose faith is strong enough, using the biblical examples of unhealed saints.
blocks.es_reference: Rechazar la distorsión de que la sanidad está garantizada a todo creyente cuya fe sea suficientemente fuerte, usando los ejemplos bíblicos de santos no sanados.

blocks.en: Locate present healing within the "now and not yet," with full healing belonging to the resurrection.
blocks.es_reference: Ubicar la sanidad presente dentro del "ya y todavía no," perteneciendo la sanidad plena a la resurrección.

blocks.en: State the biblical view of spiritual warfare — its reality, its true armor, and the errors of both denial and obsession.
blocks.es_reference: Exponer la visión bíblica de la guerra espiritual — su realidad, su verdadera armadura, y los errores tanto de la negación como de la obsesión.

blocks.en: Care for the suffering with comfort rather than blame, keeping Christ the Healer at the center.
blocks.es_reference: Cuidar al que sufre con consuelo en vez de culpa, manteniendo a Cristo el Sanador en el centro.

blocks.en: Near the Heart of the Movement
blocks.es_reference: Cerca del corazón del movimiento

blocks.en: From the very beginning, healing and the miraculous have stood near the heart of the movement we are studying. The early Pentecostals prayed for the sick and testified of recoveries; the charismatic renewal carried that expectation into the historic churches; and across the Global South today, prayer for healing and a keen sense of the spiritual battle mark much of the movement's daily life. For many believers, especially where medicine is scarce, the conviction that God still heals and still delivers is not a doctrine debated at a distance but a hope they live by.
blocks.es_reference: Desde el mismo comienzo, la sanidad y lo milagroso han estado cerca del corazón del movimiento que estudiamos. Los primeros pentecostales oraban por los enfermos y testificaban de recuperaciones; la renovación carismática llevó esa expectativa a las iglesias históricas; y por todo el Sur Global hoy, la oración por sanidad y un agudo sentido de la batalla espiritual marcan gran parte de la vida diaria del movimiento. Para muchos creyentes, especialmente donde la medicina es escasa, la convicción de que Dios todavía sana y todavía libra no es una doctrina debatida a la distancia, sino una esperanza por la cual viven.

blocks.en: So we must ask plainly what the Scriptures teach. Does God heal today? Is the gift of healing real? Is every believer promised health if only he believes? What is the nature of the spiritual conflict, and how is it to be fought? As throughout this course, we will affirm what Scripture affirms, decline what it declines, and keep two questions apart — for whether God heals is one matter, and whether healing is guaranteed on demand is quite another. And we will hold the whole subject, as we must, in submission to the Word and with Christ at the center.
blocks.es_reference: Así que debemos preguntar con claridad qué enseñan las Escrituras. ¿Sana Dios hoy? ¿Es real el don de sanidad? ¿Se promete salud a todo creyente con tal que crea? ¿Cuál es la naturaleza del conflicto espiritual, y cómo ha de librarse? Como a lo largo de este curso, afirmaremos lo que la Escritura afirma, declinaremos lo que ella declina, y mantendremos dos preguntas separadas — pues si Dios sana es un asunto, y si la sanidad está garantizada a demanda es otro muy distinto. Y sostendremos todo el tema, como debemos, en sujeción a la Palabra y con Cristo en el centro.

blocks.en: God Heals
blocks.es_reference: Dios sana

blocks.en: Begin with the great and gladdening truth: God heals. From the earliest pages of Scripture He reveals Himself as the Healer of His people — "I am the LORD who heals you" (Ex 15:26) — and the Psalms bless Him as the One "who heals all your diseases" (Ps 103:3). Sickness entered the world with the Fall and is no part of God's original design; and again and again, in His mercy, He has driven it back.
blocks.es_reference: Comencemos con la gran y gozosa verdad: Dios sana. Desde las páginas más tempranas de la Escritura Él se revela como el Sanador de su pueblo — "Yo soy Jehová tu Sanador" (Éx 15:26) — y los Salmos lo bendicen como Aquel "que sana todas tus dolencias" (Sal 103:3). La enfermedad entró en el mundo con la Caída y no es parte del diseño original de Dios; y una y otra vez, en su misericordia, Él la ha hecho retroceder.

blocks.en: In the Lord Jesus this healing mercy reached its fullness. He "went about all Galilee… healing all kinds of sickness and all kinds of disease among the people" (Matt 4:23), and Peter later summed up His ministry in a single sentence: He "went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, for God was with Him" (Acts 10:38). The apostles, in His name, healed the lame and the sick after Him. To deny that God heals would be to close our eyes to the plain testimony of Scripture and to the compassion of Christ Himself.
blocks.es_reference: En el Señor Jesús esta misericordia sanadora alcanzó su plenitud. "Recorría Jesús toda Galilea… sanando toda enfermedad y toda dolencia en el pueblo" (Mt 4:23), y Pedro después resumió su ministerio en una sola frase: "anduvo haciendo el bien, y sanando a todos los oprimidos del diablo, porque Dios estaba con Él" (Hch 10:38). Los apóstoles, en su nombre, sanaron a los cojos y a los enfermos después de Él. Negar que Dios sana sería cerrar nuestros ojos al claro testimonio de la Escritura y a la compasión de Cristo mismo.

blocks.en: The Gift of Healing and the Church's Prayer
blocks.es_reference: El don de sanidad y la oración de la iglesia

blocks.en: Nor did this healing mercy cease to touch the church. Among the gifts the Spirit distributes, Paul names "gifts of healings" (1 Cor 12:9), and James gives the church a plain instruction for the sick among its members:
blocks.es_reference: Ni cesó esta misericordia sanadora de tocar a la iglesia. Entre los dones que el Espíritu reparte, Pablo nombra "dones de sanidades" (1 Cor 12:9), y Santiago da a la iglesia una instrucción clara para los enfermos entre sus miembros:

blocks.en: "Is anyone among you sick? Let him call for the elders of the church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord. And the prayer of faith will save the sick, and the Lord will raise him up."James 5:14–15 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "¿Está alguno enfermo entre vosotros? Llame a los ancianos de la iglesia, y oren por él, ungiéndole con aceite en el nombre del Señor. Y la oración de fe salvará al enfermo, y el Señor lo levantará."Santiago 5:14–15 (RVG)

blocks.en: So the people of God are not to meet sickness with a shrug, as though healing were beneath their prayers or beyond their God. They are to pray, and to pray in faith, calling on the Lord who heals and asking Him to raise up the sick. Whether the extraordinary sign-gifts of the apostolic age continue as they were then is a question this course weighs elsewhere; but that the church should pray earnestly for the sick, and look to God to act, is beyond dispute. Where He heals, we give Him thanks; and we ask boldly, as children of a Father who delights to give good gifts.
blocks.es_reference: Así que el pueblo de Dios no ha de encarar la enfermedad con un encogimiento de hombros, como si la sanidad estuviera por debajo de sus oraciones o más allá de su Dios. Han de orar, y orar en fe, invocando al Señor que sana y pidiéndole que levante al enfermo. Si los dones de señal extraordinarios de la era apostólica continúan como entonces es una pregunta que este curso sopesa en otras partes; pero que la iglesia deba orar con fervor por los enfermos, y mirar a Dios para que actúe, está fuera de disputa. Donde Él sana, le damos gracias; y pedimos con audacia, como hijos de un Padre que se deleita en dar buenas dádivas.

blocks.en: But Not Healing on Demand
blocks.es_reference: Pero no sanidad a demanda

blocks.en: Here, however, we must speak carefully, for a real truth has been twisted into a cruel error. Some teach that every believer will always be healed if only his faith is strong enough — that health is a guaranteed right of the gospel, and that if healing does not come, the fault lies in the sick person's unbelief. This the Scriptures will not allow. They set before us godly men who prayed and were not healed, and they never once trace it to a failure of faith.
blocks.es_reference: Aquí, sin embargo, debemos hablar con cuidado, pues una verdad real ha sido torcida en un error cruel. Algunos enseñan que todo creyente siempre será sanado con tal que su fe sea suficientemente fuerte — que la salud es un derecho garantizado del evangelio, y que si la sanidad no llega, la culpa está en la incredulidad del enfermo. Esto la Escritura no lo permitirá. Nos pone delante a hombres piadosos que oraron y no fueron sanados, y ni una sola vez lo atribuye a una falta de fe.

blocks.en: Paul himself is the clearest case. Three times he begged the Lord to remove his "thorn in the flesh," and three times the answer was not the healing he sought but a greater grace:
blocks.es_reference: Pablo mismo es el caso más claro. Tres veces rogó al Señor que le quitara su "aguijón en la carne," y tres veces la respuesta no fue la sanidad que buscaba, sino una gracia mayor:

blocks.en: "My grace is sufficient for you, for My strength is made perfect in weakness."2 Corinthians 12:9 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Bástate mi gracia; porque mi poder se perfecciona en la debilidad."2 Corintios 12:9 (RVG)

blocks.en: Nor was this the only such case in Paul's own circle. He "left Trophimus in Miletus sick" (2 Tim 4:20); he told Timothy to take a little wine for his stomach and his frequent infirmities (1 Tim 5:23), counsel he would never have given had he thought the illness a mark of unbelief; and when Epaphroditus was sick "almost unto death," Paul called his recovery the mercy of God, not the reward of a formula (Phil 2:27). Even the Lord Jesus, at the pool of Bethesda, healed one man out of a multitude of the sick who lay there. Healing, then, is God's to give as He wills, in mercy — never a wage the believer earns by the strength of his believing.
blocks.es_reference: Ni fue este el único caso semejante en el propio círculo de Pablo. "A Trófimo dejé en Mileto enfermo" (2 Ti 4:20); dijo a Timoteo que tomara un poco de vino por su estómago y sus frecuentes enfermedades (1 Ti 5:23), consejo que nunca habría dado si hubiera pensado que la dolencia era una marca de incredulidad; y cuando Epafrodito estuvo enfermo "a punto de morir," Pablo llamó su recuperación la misericordia de Dios, no la recompensa de una fórmula (Flp 2:27). Aun el Señor Jesús, en el estanque de Betesda, sanó a un hombre de entre una multitud de enfermos que allí yacían. La sanidad, entonces, es de Dios para darla como Él quiere, en misericordia — nunca un salario que el creyente gana por la fuerza de su creer.

blocks.en: The Now and the Not Yet
blocks.es_reference: El ya y el todavía no

blocks.en: Why, then, does God heal some and not others now? Scripture does not give us the whole answer, but it does give us the framework in which to rest. Full and final healing — the end of all sickness, sorrow, and death itself — belongs to the resurrection and the world to come, and is promised there without exception:
blocks.es_reference: ¿Por qué, entonces, sana Dios a algunos y no a otros ahora? La Escritura no nos da toda la respuesta, pero sí nos da el marco en el cual descansar. La sanidad plena y final — el fin de toda enfermedad, tristeza, y de la muerte misma — pertenece a la resurrección y al mundo venidero, y allí se promete sin excepción:

blocks.en: "And God will wipe away every tear from their eyes; there shall be no more death, nor sorrow, nor crying. There shall be no more pain, for the former things have passed away."Revelation 21:4 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Y Dios enjugará toda lágrima de los ojos de ellos; y ya no habrá muerte, ni habrá más llanto, ni clamor, ni dolor; porque las primeras cosas pasaron."Apocalipsis 21:4 (RVG)

blocks.en: Until that day, we live in the "not yet." We "groan within ourselves, eagerly waiting for… the redemption of our body" (Rom 8:23), and our present healings, real and gracious as they are, are foretastes of that final wholeness rather than its full arrival. God may heal now, and often does, as a mercy and a sign of what is to come; but He also has purposes that suffering can serve — the perfecting of His strength in our weakness, the deepening of our trust, and, as with the man born blind, the display of His own works (John 9:3). The believer who is not yet healed has not been failed by God; he is waiting, with all creation, for a healing that is sure.
blocks.es_reference: Hasta aquel día, vivimos en el "todavía no." "Gemimos dentro de nosotros mismos, esperando… la redención de nuestro cuerpo" (Ro 8:23), y nuestras sanidades presentes, reales y llenas de gracia como son, son anticipos de aquella plenitud final más que su llegada completa. Dios puede sanar ahora, y a menudo lo hace, como una misericordia y una señal de lo que ha de venir; pero también tiene propósitos que el sufrimiento puede servir — el perfeccionar su fuerza en nuestra debilidad, el ahondar de nuestra confianza, y, como con el ciego de nacimiento, la manifestación de sus propias obras (Jn 9:3). El creyente que aún no ha sido sanado no ha sido fallado por Dios; espera, con toda la creación, una sanidad que es segura.

blocks.en: Miracles and the Sign-Seeking Heart
blocks.es_reference: Los milagros y el corazón que busca señales

blocks.en: What is true of healing is true of the miraculous more broadly. God is sovereign over His creation and is able to do wonders; nothing in Scripture shuts His hand. The signs and wonders of the apostolic age served to attest the gospel as it was first preached, God "bearing witness both with signs and wonders" (Heb 2:4). Whether such sign-gifts continue in the same manner today is the open question weighed in other units, and we do not settle it here; but that God still acts, still answers prayer, and can heal beyond human explanation, we gladly affirm.
blocks.es_reference: Lo que es cierto de la sanidad es cierto de lo milagroso más ampliamente. Dios es soberano sobre su creación y es capaz de hacer maravillas; nada en la Escritura cierra su mano. Las señales y los prodigios de la era apostólica sirvieron para atestiguar el evangelio tal como fue predicado por primera vez, "testificando Dios con señales y prodigios" (Heb 2:4). Si tales dones de señal continúan de la misma manera hoy es la pregunta abierta sopesada en otras unidades, y no la resolvemos aquí; pero que Dios todavía actúa, todavía responde la oración, y puede sanar más allá de la explicación humana, lo afirmamos con gozo.

blocks.en: Yet Scripture also warns against a certain hunger for the miraculous. "An evil and adulterous generation seeks after a sign," the Lord said (Matt 12:39), rebuking those who wanted wonders more than they wanted God. A heart set on signs can drift from the Giver to the gifts, prizing the spectacular over the Savior and measuring faith by marvels rather than by obedience and love. We are to seek God Himself, to trust Him whether or not He grants the wonder we ask, and to remember that the greatest miracle is not a healed body but a saved and changed soul.
blocks.es_reference: Sin embargo, la Escritura también advierte contra cierta hambre de lo milagroso. "La generación mala y adúltera demanda señal," dijo el Señor (Mt 12:39), reprendiendo a los que querían maravillas más de lo que querían a Dios. Un corazón puesto en las señales puede derivar del Dador a los dones, prefiriendo lo espectacular al Salvador y midiendo la fe por prodigios en vez de por la obediencia y el amor. Hemos de buscar a Dios mismo, confiar en Él conceda o no la maravilla que pedimos, y recordar que el mayor milagro no es un cuerpo sanado, sino un alma salvada y transformada.

blocks.en: The Reality of Spiritual Warfare
blocks.es_reference: La realidad de la guerra espiritual

blocks.en: Alongside healing, the movement has always taken seriously the reality of spiritual warfare, and in this it is right, for Scripture is plain that the Christian life is a battle. There is a real enemy, the devil, and there are real spiritual powers of evil arrayed against the people of God:
blocks.es_reference: Junto a la sanidad, el movimiento siempre ha tomado en serio la realidad de la guerra espiritual, y en esto tiene razón, pues la Escritura es clara en que la vida cristiana es una batalla. Hay un enemigo real, el diablo, y hay poderes espirituales reales de maldad dispuestos contra el pueblo de Dios:

blocks.en: "For we do not wrestle against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this age, against spiritual hosts of wickedness in the heavenly places."Ephesians 6:12 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Porque no tenemos lucha contra sangre y carne, sino contra principados, contra potestades, contra los gobernadores de las tinieblas de este mundo, contra huestes espirituales de maldad en las regiones celestes."Efesios 6:12 (RVG)

blocks.en: We do not fight, then, merely against human opponents or against our own weakness; behind these stands a spiritual adversary, cunning and malicious, who "walks about like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour" (1 Pet 5:8). To pretend otherwise, to treat the spiritual realm as a fable, is to be caught unaware in a war that is really being waged. The believer must be sober and watchful, and must not be ignorant of the enemy's devices.
blocks.es_reference: No luchamos, entonces, meramente contra oponentes humanos ni contra nuestra propia debilidad; detrás de estos está un adversario espiritual, astuto y malicioso, que "anda alrededor como león rugiente, buscando a quien devorar" (1 P 5:8). Fingir lo contrario, tratar el reino espiritual como una fábula, es ser tomado por sorpresa en una guerra que realmente se está librando. El creyente debe ser sobrio y velar, y no debe ignorar las maquinaciones del enemigo.

blocks.en: Warfare in Biblical Proportion
blocks.es_reference: La guerra en proporción bíblica

blocks.en: But Scripture also keeps this warfare in careful proportion, and here the movement has sometimes stumbled. The armor God gives is not a set of techniques, formulas, or sensational rituals; it is truth, righteousness, the readiness of the gospel, faith, salvation, the Word of God, and prayer (Eph 6:14–18). Victory is not wrung from the enemy by the right words or the loudest voice; it is Christ's, who "disarmed principalities and powers" at the cross and made a public spectacle of them (Col 2:15). "Resist the devil," James writes, "and he will flee from you" (James 4:7), and John assures us, "He who is in you is greater than he who is in the world" (1 John 4:4).
blocks.es_reference: Pero la Escritura también mantiene esta guerra en cuidadosa proporción, y aquí el movimiento a veces ha tropezado. La armadura que Dios da no es un conjunto de técnicas, fórmulas o rituales sensacionalistas; es la verdad, la justicia, la disposición del evangelio, la fe, la salvación, la Palabra de Dios y la oración (Ef 6:14–18). La victoria no se arranca del enemigo con las palabras correctas ni con la voz más fuerte; es de Cristo, quien "despojando a los principados y a las potestades" en la cruz los exhibió públicamente (Col 2:15). "Resistid al diablo," escribe Santiago, "y huirá de vosotros" (Stg 4:7), y Juan nos asegura: "mayor es el que está en vosotros, que el que está en el mundo" (1 Jn 4:4).

blocks.en: So we avoid the two opposite errors. On one side is the denial that dismisses the demonic as unreal; on the other is the obsession that finds a demon behind every illness, every sin, and every misfortune, and that gives the devil more attention and more credit than Scripture ever does. To blame all our troubles on evil spirits is to excuse our own sin and to forget the ordinary weakness of the flesh and the pull of the world. The believer's confidence is not in his skill at spiritual combat but in his Lord; he keeps the enemy in view, but he keeps Christ at the center, and it is Christ, not the devil, who fills his thoughts and his praise.
blocks.es_reference: Así que evitamos los dos errores opuestos. De un lado está la negación que descarta lo demoníaco como irreal; del otro está la obsesión que halla un demonio detrás de cada enfermedad, cada pecado y cada desgracia, y que da al diablo más atención y más crédito de lo que la Escritura jamás le da. Culpar de todos nuestros males a los espíritus malignos es excusar nuestro propio pecado y olvidar la debilidad ordinaria de la carne y la atracción del mundo. La confianza del creyente no está en su destreza en el combate espiritual, sino en su Señor; mantiene al enemigo a la vista, pero mantiene a Cristo en el centro, y es Cristo, no el diablo, quien llena sus pensamientos y su alabanza.

blocks.en: The Pastoral Wound
blocks.es_reference: La herida pastoral

blocks.en: As with the prosperity teaching, the errors around healing are not merely mistaken; they wound. Picture the believer, already bearing the weight of a long illness, who is told that his sickness lingers because his faith is too weak — or the grieving family informed that their loved one died for want of believing. To the pain of the body such teaching adds the pain of false guilt, and it slanders the God who is nearest to the broken.
blocks.es_reference: Como con la enseñanza de la prosperidad, los errores en torno a la sanidad no son meramente equivocados; hieren. Imagine al creyente, ya cargando el peso de una larga enfermedad, a quien se le dice que su enfermedad persiste porque su fe es demasiado débil — o a la familia en duelo informada de que su ser querido murió por falta de creer. Al dolor del cuerpo tal enseñanza añade el dolor de la culpa falsa, y calumnia al Dios que está más cerca del quebrantado.

blocks.en: The Scriptures speak a kinder and truer word. "The LORD is near to those who have a broken heart" (Ps 34:18). Paul's thorn remained, and God's grace was enough. A faithful shepherd will pray earnestly for the healing of his people, and will use every ordinary mercy of medicine and care without shame — for Luke, the beloved physician, was Paul's own companion, and wine was Timothy's prescribed remedy. But he will never lay upon the suffering the crushing burden of blame; he will comfort them with the presence of God and the sufficiency of His grace.
blocks.es_reference: Las Escrituras hablan una palabra más bondadosa y más verdadera. "Cercano está Jehová a los quebrantados de corazón" (Sal 34:18). El aguijón de Pablo permaneció, y la gracia de Dios fue suficiente. Un pastor fiel orará con fervor por la sanidad de su gente, y usará toda misericordia ordinaria de la medicina y el cuidado sin vergüenza — pues Lucas, el médico amado, fue el propio compañero de Pablo, y el vino fue el remedio recetado de Timoteo. Pero nunca pondrá sobre el que sufre la carga aplastante de la culpa; los consolará con la presencia de Dios y la suficiencia de su gracia.

blocks.en: Holding It Together: Christ the Healer
blocks.es_reference: Sosteniéndolo junto: Cristo el Sanador

blocks.en: How, then, shall we hold all this together? We pray boldly for the sick, expecting God to act, and we anoint and lay on hands as James directs. We use the ordinary means God has given, thanking Him for medicine and skill as His gifts. We submit our asking to His will, praying as the leper did, "Lord, if You are willing" (Matt 8:2), and as our Lord Himself did in the garden, "not My will, but Yours." We take the spiritual battle seriously, but in biblical proportion, resting in Christ's finished victory. And we comfort the afflicted rather than condemning them.
blocks.es_reference: ¿Cómo, entonces, sostendremos todo esto junto? Oramos con audacia por los enfermos, esperando que Dios actúe, y ungimos e imponemos las manos como Santiago manda. Usamos los medios ordinarios que Dios ha dado, dándole gracias por la medicina y la destreza como sus dones. Sometemos nuestro pedir a su voluntad, orando como el leproso lo hizo: "Señor, si quieres" (Mt 8:2), y como nuestro Señor mismo lo hizo en el huerto: "no se haga mi voluntad, sino la tuya." Tomamos en serio la batalla espiritual, pero en proporción bíblica, descansando en la victoria consumada de Cristo. Y consolamos al afligido en vez de condenarlo.

blocks.en: Through it all we remember that the Healer is the Savior, and that the aim of every healing and every deliverance is to glorify Him and to point beyond itself — to the greater healing of the soul from sin, and to the final healing of the resurrection, when He will wipe away every tear. He may heal the body now, in mercy; He will heal it fully then, in glory; and in life or in death, in sickness or in health, He Himself is the believer's hope.
blocks.es_reference: A través de todo ello recordamos que el Sanador es el Salvador, y que el fin de toda sanidad y toda liberación es glorificarlo a Él y señalar más allá de sí misma — a la sanidad mayor del alma del pecado, y a la sanidad final de la resurrección, cuando Él enjugará toda lágrima. Él puede sanar el cuerpo ahora, en misericordia; lo sanará plenamente entonces, en gloria; y en la vida o en la muerte, en la enfermedad o en la salud, Él mismo es la esperanza del creyente.

blocks.en: Looking Ahead
blocks.es_reference: Mirando adelante

blocks.en: In the next unit we take up the questions that have run beneath much of this study and press them directly: whether prophecy and tongues continue in the church today, and how any such gift relates to the closed and completed Scriptures. We will set out the strongest case on each side and, as ever, weigh it by the Word.
blocks.es_reference: En la próxima unidad tomamos las preguntas que han corrido debajo de gran parte de este estudio y las planteamos directamente: si la profecía y las lenguas continúan en la iglesia hoy, y cómo se relaciona cualquier don semejante con las Escrituras cerradas y completadas. Expondremos el caso más fuerte de cada lado y, como siempre, lo sopesaremos por la Palabra.

blocks.en: Discussion Questions
blocks.es_reference: Preguntas para discusión

blocks.en: How can a church pray boldly for healing while also submitting to God's will?
blocks.es_reference: ¿Cómo puede una iglesia orar con audacia por sanidad y a la vez someterse a la voluntad de Dios?

blocks.en: Why is it both untrue and cruel to tell a sick believer that his illness proves weak faith?
blocks.es_reference: ¿Por qué es a la vez falso y cruel decirle a un creyente enfermo que su enfermedad prueba una fe débil?

blocks.en: What examples from Scripture keep us from believing that healing is guaranteed on demand?

mc.stem: On healing, Scripture teaches that God —
options: never heals anyone today
is the LORD who heals, and the church is to pray for the sick, expecting Him to act
guarantees every believer perfect health
heals only apostles
mc.why: Scripture affirms God as Healer (Ex 15:26; Ps 103:3) and commands the church to pray for the sick (James 5:14–15); the gift of healings is real.

mc.stem: James 5:14–15 directs that when a believer is sick —
options: he should hide his illness
he should demand healing as his right
he should call for the elders to pray over him and anoint him with oil
he should never see a physician
mc.why: The church is to pray in faith for the sick; healing is sought from the Lord, who raises up as He wills.

mc.stem: The distortion this unit rejects is the teaching that —
options: every believer will always be healed if only his faith is strong enough, so that continued sickness proves unbelief
God is able to heal
the church should pray for the sick
Christ had compassion on the suffering
mc.why: Scripture shows godly people who were not healed — Paul's thorn, Trophimus, Timothy, Epaphroditus — so healing is God's to give as He wills, never a wage owed to sufficient faith.

mc.stem: That Paul's thorn was not removed, and that he left Trophimus sick, shows that —
options: Paul lacked faith
healing is always guaranteed
sickness is always sin
even the most faithful are not always healed, and healing is given according to God's will
mc.why: God's grace was sufficient for Paul; full and final healing belongs to the resurrection, while now God heals as He wills, in mercy.

mc.stem: On spiritual warfare, Scripture teaches that —
options: there is no real spiritual enemy
the battle is real, but the believer's armor is truth, righteousness, the gospel, faith, salvation, the Word, and prayer — not techniques or sensational rituals
every sin and illness should be blamed on a demon
believers should fear the devil more than they trust Christ
mc.why: Ephesians 6 describes a real conflict fought with biblical armor; Christ has disarmed the powers (Col 2:15), and the enemy flees when resisted (James 4:7).

mc.stem: How should the church treat a believer who is not healed despite prayer?
options: tell him his faith was too weak
conclude he has hidden sin
stop praying for anyone
comfort him, assure him of God's nearness and sufficient grace, and never blame him for his suffering
mc.why: To blame the afflicted for their affliction adds cruelty to grief; God is near the brokenhearted, and His grace is sufficient even when the thorn remains.

mc.stem: This unit's balanced position on healing and warfare is to —
options: deny that God heals or that evil spirits exist
guarantee healing and hunt demons behind every trouble
affirm that God heals and the battle is real, while rejecting guaranteed-healing and demon-obsession, and keeping Christ at the center
ignore the subject entirely
mc.why: The unit holds both truths together: God heals and the spiritual battle is real, yet neither is a formula; the aim of every healing and victory is to glorify Christ.

sa.prompt: State what this unit affirms about God's healing and what distortion it rejects.
sa.model: This unit affirms that God heals — He is the Lord who heals, the gift of healings is real, and the church is commanded to pray for the sick and anoint them, expecting the Lord to act. What it rejects is the distortion of guaranteed healing — the teaching that every believer will always be healed if only his faith is strong enough, so that continued sickness becomes proof of unbelief. Scripture shows godly people who were not healed, which teaches that healing is God's to give according to His will, in mercy, and is never a wage owed to sufficient faith.

sa.prompt: Give three examples from Scripture of faithful people who were not healed, and explain what they teach.
sa.model: Scripture gives several examples. Paul asked three times for his thorn in the flesh to be removed, but it was not; the answer was that God's grace was sufficient for him. Paul left Trophimus sick at Miletus, and he told Timothy to take a little wine for his frequent stomach ailments rather than rebuking him for unbelief. These teach that even the most faithful are not always healed now, that sickness is no proof of unbelief, and that full and final healing belongs to the resurrection, while now God heals as He wills according to His will.

sa.prompt: Summarize the biblical view of spiritual warfare, including what to affirm and what to avoid.
sa.model: The biblical view affirms that spiritual warfare is real: there is a genuine enemy, the devil, and real forces of evil, and the Christian life is a battle. But the armor Scripture gives is truth, righteousness, the gospel, faith, salvation, the Word, and prayer — not techniques or sensational rituals. What we avoid is blaming every sin, illness, or misfortune on a demon, and a preoccupation with the demonic that eclipses Christ. Victory belongs to Christ, who disarmed the powers; the believer resists the enemy, stays sober and watchful, and keeps the Savior, not the devil, at the center.

sa.prompt: Why do healing and the miraculous stand near the heart of the movement, and what two questions does the unit keep apart?
sa.model: The early Pentecostals prayed for the sick and testified of recoveries, the charismatic renewal carried that expectation into the historic churches, and across the Global South prayer for healing and a keen sense of the spiritual battle mark the movement's daily life; for many believers, especially where medicine is scarce, the conviction that God still heals and delivers is not a doctrine debated at a distance but a hope they live by. The two questions kept apart are whether God heals, which is one matter, and whether healing is guaranteed on demand, which is quite another.

sa.prompt: Show from Scripture that God heals, from Exodus through the ministry of Jesus and the apostles.
sa.model: God reveals Himself as the Healer of His people, 'I am the LORD who heals you' (Exodus 15:26), and the Psalms bless Him as the One 'who heals all your diseases' (Psalm 103:3); sickness entered with the Fall and is no part of God's original design, and again and again He has driven it back. In Jesus this mercy reached its fullness: He went about all Galilee healing all kinds of sickness and disease, and Peter summed up His ministry as going about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil (Acts 10:38). The apostles healed the lame and the sick in His name after Him. To deny that God heals is to close our eyes to Scripture and to the compassion of Christ.

sa.prompt: What does James 5:14–15 instruct, and what does the unit say the church must not do in the face of sickness?
sa.model: The sick are to call for the elders of the church, who pray over them and anoint them with oil in the name of the Lord; the prayer of faith will save the sick and the Lord will raise him up. Paul also names 'gifts of healings' among the Spirit's gifts. So the people of God are not to meet sickness with a shrug, as though healing were beneath their prayers or beyond their God; they are to pray in faith and look to God to act, asking boldly as children of a Father who delights to give good gifts, and giving thanks where He heals. Whether the extraordinary sign-gifts continue as in the apostolic age is weighed elsewhere.

sa.prompt: How does the 'now and not yet' framework answer why God heals some and not others now?
sa.model: Full and final healing, the end of all sickness, sorrow, and death, belongs to the resurrection and the world to come and is promised there without exception: God will wipe away every tear (Revelation 21:4). Until then we live in the not yet, groaning within ourselves and waiting for the redemption of our body (Romans 8:23), and present healings, real and gracious, are foretastes of that wholeness rather than its full arrival. God may heal now as a mercy and a sign, but He also has purposes suffering can serve: the perfecting of His strength in weakness, the deepening of trust, and, as with the man born blind, the display of His works (John 9:3). The believer not yet healed has not been failed by God; he is waiting, with all creation, for a healing that is sure.

sa.prompt: What warning does Scripture give against a sign-seeking heart, and what is the greatest miracle?
sa.model: God is sovereign and able to do wonders; the signs of the apostolic age attested the gospel as it was first preached (Hebrews 2:4), and God still acts, answers prayer, and can heal beyond explanation. Yet 'an evil and adulterous generation seeks after a sign' (Matthew 12:39), the Lord's rebuke of those who wanted wonders more than they wanted God. A heart set on signs drifts from the Giver to the gifts, prizes the spectacular over the Savior, and measures faith by marvels rather than by obedience and love. We seek God Himself, trust Him whether or not He grants the wonder, and remember that the greatest miracle is not a healed body but a saved and changed soul.

sa.prompt: What is the armor God gives for spiritual warfare, and where does victory come from?
sa.model: The armor is not a set of techniques, formulas, or sensational rituals; it is truth, righteousness, the readiness of the gospel, faith, salvation, the Word of God, and prayer (Ephesians 6:14–18). Victory is not wrung from the enemy by the right words or the loudest voice; it is Christ's, who disarmed principalities and powers at the cross and made a public spectacle of them (Colossians 2:15). 'Resist the devil and he will flee from you' (James 4:7), and 'He who is in you is greater than he who is in the world' (1 John 4:4); the believer's confidence is not in his skill at spiritual combat but in his Lord.

sa.prompt: Describe the 'pastoral wound' the errors around healing inflict, and how the unit says the shepherd should respond.
sa.model: A believer bearing a long illness is told it lingers because his faith is too weak, or a grieving family is informed their loved one died for want of believing; to the pain of the body such teaching adds false guilt, and it slanders the God who is nearest to the broken. The Scriptures speak a kinder, truer word: the LORD is near to those who have a broken heart, Paul's thorn remained and God's grace was enough. A faithful shepherd prays earnestly for healing, uses every ordinary mercy of medicine and care without shame, since Luke the physician was Paul's companion and wine was Timothy's prescribed remedy, but never lays on the suffering the crushing burden of blame; he comforts them with the presence of God and the sufficiency of His grace.
